title: Scanning Networks

objectives.text: Explain how scanning follows footprinting and map it to ATT&CK T1595 and T1046
Describe the TCP three-way handshake, the six TCP flags and the ICMP types used in scanning
Match each host discovery probe (ARP, ICMP, TCP, UDP) with the reply that proves a host is up
Interpret open, closed, filtered, unfiltered, open|filtered and closed|filtered for each Nmap scan type
Recognise Nmap, hping3 and other scanners by name, purpose and output
Tell active from passive OS fingerprinting and read TTL and banner clues
Recognise the evasion concept classes (fragmentation, decoys, spoofing, idle scan, slow timing) and how each is detected
Pair each scanning technique with its countermeasure and its detection signal

readingMap.why: Handshake, flags, ICMP types and port ranges underpin every other question; know the step order and ATT&CK names.
Know which probe each option sends and what reply means 'up'; -sn vs -Pn is a classic.
Scan types and the reply behind each port state are the single most tested topic of the module.
Active vs passive, TTL rounding and banners; skip the fingerprint format details.
Recognise each concept class and what it hides; the defender's detection is what matters.
Match each technique to its countermeasure and detection; scenario questions come from here.
